To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students' academic and extracurricular involvement during the transition period affects their grades and satisfaction with college, that minority students' involvement in extracollegiate activities is especially important for their academic and social adjustment, and that negative perceptions of the racial climate of their campus are detrimental to their satisfaction and increase their likelihood of leaving.
minority and white students differ in their academic and social involvement, which affects their grades, overall satisfaction, and likelihood of leaving college.

1) minority students benefit more from involvement in extrarricular activities than white students do; 2) minority students who are involved in academic activities are less likely to leave college than those who are not; 3) minority students who have a positive view of the campus racial climate are more likely to be satisfied with college; and 4) minority students who perceive the campus racial climate as negative are more likely to leave college.

the role of race and ethnicity in the college experience.
